page: Google Cloud Platform n2d-standard-2 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance based on the x86_64 architecture. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs powered by an AMD EPYC 7B13 processor, consisting of 1 physical core with 2 threads. The instance is equipped with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It does not include bundled local storage or GPU accelerators. The processor features 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware support for AVX, AES, VAES, and SHA_NI cryptographic instructions.

Benchmark data reveals a distinct performance profile. The instance demonstrates strong single-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests, placing in the top 25%. However, multi-core CPU performance falls into the bottom 25%, and Geekbench multi-core scores are in the bottom 10%. Memory performance is a notable bottleneck, with read-only small block cached bandwidth and Passmark memory scores both ranking in the bottom 10%. Large block read and write speeds also remain weak, falling in the bottom 25%. Single-threaded tasks like gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at an average level, while complex tasks such as ray tracing, image processing, and software compilation with clang show poor performance in the bottom 10%.

From a resource density perspective, this instance offers a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, representing an entry-level tier for dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources. Given the weak multi-core scaling and low memory bandwidth, it is best suited for lightweight, single-threaded workloads, basic text processing, and low-traffic static web serving. It is not recommended for database operations, multi-threaded compilation, or memory-bound applications due to poor benchmark results in those areas.
